question: Check count-only evidence coverage for daridorexant in pregnancy across PubMed, ClinicalTrials.gov, DailyMed, LactMed and MPRINT. Explain what each count does and does not establish.
criteria: Use count-only probes. LactMed is lactation-only and not applicable to pregnancy. Do not equate counts or zero matches with evidence quality or safety. Preserve unknown versus zero.
answer:
## Count-only coverage for daridorexant in pregnancy

These counts are navigation results only. They are not comparable across sources and do not establish safety, evidence quality, study findings, or absence of evidence elsewhere.

| Source | Count | What the count indicates | What it does not establish |
|---|---:|---|---|
| **PubMed** | **3** | Three matches to the returned daridorexant-and-pregnancy search. | The matches may not represent distinct studies, human pregnancy research, or reports containing pregnancy outcomes. They do not establish study quality or findings. The attempted daridorexant MeSH term was not found in the returned search metadata. [S4](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/) |
| **ClinicalTrials.gov** | **4** | Four registration matches for `daridorexant AND (pregnancy)`. | The count does not establish enrollment, current recruitment, posted results, outcomes, or applicability to a particular gestational age or population. [S1](https://clinicaltrials.gov/) |
| **DailyMed** | **1** | One name-matched product-label record. | It does not establish that the record contains a pregnancy-specific section, current approval status for a particular use, or independent clinical evidence. [S2](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/) |
| **LactMed** | **Not applicable** | LactMed is a lactation-only resource, so no pregnancy count was supplied. [S6](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK501922/) | It cannot provide pregnancy evidence or general pediatric evidence. The lookup did not identify a curated federal pregnancy counterpart to LactMed; this is a limitation of this source review, not proof that none exists. [S5](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/labeling/questions-and-answers-pregnancy-and-lactation-labeling-rule) [S6](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK501922/) |
| **MPRINT Gold snapshot** | **0** literal drug-name row matches; **0** distinct PMIDs | No literal daridorexant matches were found in the selected MPRINT Gold snapshot tables. Snapshot date: **November 17, 2026**; revision `4bdee90dff3610816e86d0eed29b4c4d0fe76e89`. | This does not prove that no relevant publication exists. The MCP reports that this count is limited to selected snapshot tables and literal-name matching; rows are not necessarily distinct studies, and the count does not assess outcomes. [S3](https://github.com/langli-lab/mprint-kp-data) |

### Bottom line

This count-only lookup found searchable matches in PubMed, ClinicalTrials.gov, and DailyMed, while LactMed was not applicable to pregnancy and MPRINT returned no literal-name Gold matches in the specified snapshot. **No clinical evidence was reviewed, and the results do not establish safety or lack of safety.**
